subject.title: Feature: inbound 'reply in thread' / 'rit' user directive

question: Should OpenClaw core treat suffixes like `reply in thread` or `rit` as a built-in cross-channel reply override, and what trigger vocabulary plus `replyToMode` behavior should be accepted by default?
rationale: Source inspection shows the feature is absent, but adding global natural-language parsing can silently change message routing and may introduce public config behavior.

options.title: Approve narrow core directive
options.body: Adopt only unambiguous suffixes, likely excluding bare `thread`, and require stripping from all model-facing and command-facing inbound bodies with defined reply-mode override behavior.

options.title: Keep it prompt or plugin owned
options.body: Leave natural-language phrasing to agent instructions or a future plugin/API seam and keep core limited to explicit reply tags plus configured reply modes.

options.title: Require default-off config first
options.body: Allow the behavior only behind documented schema/config with focused upgrade-safe tests and no default routing change for existing installs.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow core directive
recommendation.body: Adopt only unambiguous suffixes, likely excluding bare `thread`, and require stripping from all model-facing and command-facing inbound bodies with defined reply-mode override behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest historical signal for inbound context finalization and shared reply threading points to steipete-authored commits, making him the best available product-routing owner from the inspected history.
